page: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance architected on the Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8275CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, offering 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. System memory comprises 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. Machine learning execution is offloaded to 16 AWS Inferentia accelerator chips containing a cumulative 128 GB of VRAM. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 100 Gbps, while local instance storage is absent, necessitating network-attached volumes for persistent file systems.

Synthetic CPU and memory benchmarks reflect strong aggregate throughput. The server registered a multi-core stress-ng metric of 94571.8 and a PassMark CPU score of 62408.52, both placing in the top quartile of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 232.48 GB/sec with write speeds of 97.87 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates high concurrency handling, highlighted by 79.6 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 43.52 GB/sec. Single-core performance remains moderate, with Geekbench and stress-ng scores settling in the middle 50% band.

Evaluation of language model tasks illustrates clear architectural tradeoffs. Small and medium model prompt processing speeds achieve average marks, yet text generation throughput drops into the bottom 10%, generating 40.73 tokens per second on a 135M model and 5.46 tokens per second on a 7B model. Cost efficiency is centered around dense Inferentia hardware utilization rather than open-ended autoregressive token generation. Consequently, the inf1.24xlarge is best matched with conventional deep learning inference, image recognition, multi-threaded batch preprocessing, and microservice architectures requiring high network bandwidth and specialized accelerator density.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor, engineered for machine learning inference and high-throughput compute workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with dedicated allocation, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz. Acceleration is delivered via 16 AWS Inferentia chips supplying 128 GB of aggregate VRAM. Networking throughput reaches a baseline of 100 Gbps, though no local storage is included, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark testing indicates strong multi-core processing, memory bandwidth exceeding 232 GB/sec uncached read, and high Redis and web throughput. However, LLM text generation benchmarks place in the bottom decile, contrasting with average prompt processing throughput. The inf1.24xlarge offers dense hardware-accelerated capacity suited for scaled model inference pipelines, batch processing, and high-concurrency microservices, while trading off local disk storage and generative text throughput.
